topDown.potential: Direct access to the decision-making level, without going through an intermediate relay.
topDown.prereq: An identified contact at decision-maker level, and a reason to write to them directly.
topDown.limits: A longer cycle: a decision-maker rarely delegates a first reply.
topDown.workload: Few messages to prepare, but each demands careful preparation: a decision-maker won't forgive a generic approach.
topDown.paybackDelay: The signal comes quickly or not at all: past two follow-ups with no response, this path won't open.
topDown.risk: The risk: an approach perceived as too direct closes access for a long time. Signal to watch: a message read with no reply and no acknowledgement.
topDown.firstTest: One outreach at decision-maker level on a priority account, and see if it gets a reply.
topDown.stopCondition: No reply after two spaced follow-ups: switch path rather than insist.

bottomUp.potential: An entry point that stays reachable even without an identified decision-maker.
bottomUp.prereq: An operational entry point able to raise the need internally.
bottomUp.limits: The deal can stall before it reaches whoever decides.
bottomUp.workload: Extra exchanges needed to raise the need internally, before reaching whoever decides.
bottomUp.paybackDelay: The return depends on how long the operational contact takes to relay internally.
bottomUp.risk: The risk: the deal stays at operational level and never moves up. Signal to watch: the contact names no one above them after several exchanges.
bottomUp.firstTest: One exchange with an operational contact, and see if they can name who decides.
bottomUp.stopCondition: No decision-maker named after three exchanges: reconsider entering from the top.

multiThread.potential: Several entry points on the same account: one closed door doesn't stop the deal.
multiThread.prereq: Several identifiable contacts at the same account, at different levels.
multiThread.limits: More messages to personalise, and more follow-up to keep the threads consistent with each other.
multiThread.workload: Each thread is personalised and followed up separately, which adds coordination work.
multiThread.paybackDelay: Varies from one thread to another: some move while others stay silent.
multiThread.risk: The risk: inconsistent messages if the threads aren't kept in sync. Signal to watch: two contacts at the same account report different versions.
multiThread.firstTest: Two outreaches on the same account, at two levels, and see which one moves.
multiThread.stopCondition: No thread moves after the first exchange: focus the effort on a single one.

referral.potential: The trust of the relationship making the introduction carries the first contact.
referral.prereq: An existing relationship — client, partner or contact — ready to make the introduction.
referral.limits: Cannot be triggered on demand: it depends on a relationship that already exists.
referral.workload: A single message to prepare: the one addressed to the relationship making the introduction.
referral.paybackDelay: Depends on the schedule of the relationship making the introduction, outside the rep's direct control.
referral.risk: The risk: the relationship has neither the time nor the occasion to make the introduction. Signal to watch: no news of the requested introduction after a polite follow-up.
referral.firstTest: One introduction requested from an existing relationship on a priority account.
referral.stopCondition: No introduction made after a follow-up: return to a path that doesn't depend on a third party.
